correctness.rationale: For \(S_{m,n}=K_m\vee\overline{K_n}\), every zero on the independent side sees exactly the clique weight \(c\). If \(q>0\), Italian domination forces \(c\ge2\). Defending one such zero lowers clique weight by one; when \(q=1\) no independent zero remains, while for \(q\ge2\) another independent zero remains and forces \(c-1\ge2\), giving the sharp \(c\ge3\) threshold. When \(q=0\), clique zeros are secure if \(c>0\); if \(c=0\), moving from an independent label two is valid whereas moving from label one creates an undefended independent zero. The three disjoint regimes yield the displayed weight enumerator. Fresh exhaustive checks on \((m,n)=(1,2),(1,3),(2,2),(2,3),(3,2)\) matched the criterion for every ternary labeling.
residual_risks: The theorem excludes the complete-graph boundary \(n=1\).
